harness: Each row's example runs in this harness: `container` is the timeline's element, `items` five items over March 2026 in two lanes (`lanes`), `DAY` a day in milliseconds. `before` runs before `createTimeline`, `config` goes into its configuration, `after` runs with `timeline`. Every plugin is registered first (`registerPlugin` with the Gantt chart, the resource view, export, the time tools, groups, item kinds and other languages), as a page moving from vis-timeline would: vis-timeline draws all of its features without asking. Register only the ones your configuration uses, and a page loads only those.

statuses.renamed: Same meaning, another name or place.
statuses.different: Possible, done another way — read the note.

rows.note: Plain arrays, no DataSet. One configuration object holds everything.

`@temporeum/timeline-core/vis-compat` reads vis-timeline's items, groups and options by vis-timeline's own rules — date strings as moment reads them, item types, nested and hidden groups, `groupOrder` — and returns the configuration, and a warning for everything that did not carry over.
Items are immutable data: hand the timeline the next array. For data that is too big to hold, `items` can be a function that loads a window.
rows.after: timeline.setItems([...items, { id: "extra", start: new Date("2026-03-12"), label: "Added", laneId: "work" }]);

rows.note: A key given as `undefined` goes back to its default; a key left out keeps its value.
The timeline follows its container's size. Below `breakpoint` it turns vertical when `orientation` is `"auto"`.

rows.after:
timeline.destroy();
if (!timeline.destroyed) throw new Error("still alive");

rows.note: Without a domain the view fits the items, with a margin.

rows.config: limits: { min: new Date("2026-01-01"), max: new Date("2026-12-31") }

rows.note: The shortest and longest visible span, in milliseconds.
The snapshot is also what `subscribe` listeners read: it fits React's `useSyncExternalStore`.
rows.after:
const [start, end] = timeline.getSnapshot().domain;
console.log(new Date(start), new Date(end));

rows.note: A factor above 1 zooms in. `around` is the time that stays put; the centre by default.
There is no `fit()`: the first view fits the items when no `domain` is given; later, zoom to their extent.
Fixed, not an option: a plain wheel pans or scrolls, ctrl + wheel (and a trackpad pinch, which browsers report as one) zooms.
A plain wheel already pans along time and scrolls the lanes. On touch, `"cooperative"` leaves vertical page scrolling to the page, for a timeline inside an article.
The view keeps its span and keeps now at `offset` (the middle by default), reading the clock every `intervalMs`. A pan or a zoom of the reader's lets go of it; `follow()` picks it up again.
rows.after: timeline.addItems([{ id: "now", start: Date.now(), label: "Now", laneId: "work" }]);

rows.note: The same shape. `start` and `end` are `Date`s or epoch milliseconds, and a repeat is a calendar repeat in `timeZone`: a nightly range stays on the wall clock across a change of daylight saving.
rows.config: hiddenDates: [{ start: new Date("2026-03-07"), end: new Date("2026-03-09"), repeat: "weekly" }]

rows.note: A number of CSS pixels. Without one, the container's own height when a stylesheet gives it one.
The timeline fills its container; size the container.
Spacing comes in three densities, picked automatically by default to fit the items.
Not to be confused with Temporeum's `orientation`, which is horizontal or vertical.
`"pack"` (the default) is vis's `stack: true`; `"single"` gives every item its own row. Also per lane.
Labels start at the item's start, and move after it when they do not fit inside.
Sanitised by default: scripts, handlers and anything outside an allow-list are dropped (`templateOptions`). For full control over the SVG, `hooks.renderItem` returns scene nodes.
A cluster is one keyboard stop that opens into its items.
Labels and tooltips are text, never HTML. A `template` is HTML, run through the library's own sanitiser unless `templateOptions.sanitize` is `false`.
rows.after: timeline.setItems([{ id: "x", laneId: "work", start: new Date("2026-03-10"), label: "" }]);

rows.note: A BCP 47 tag, through `Intl`. `timeZone` sets the zone the axis is drawn in.

Month and day names come from `Intl` for any `locale`. The timeline's own words — its name, the zoom buttons, "New item" — come from a dictionary: `strings` over `DEFAULT_STRINGS` (`@temporeum/timeline-core/intl`).
One function for every tick label; `tick.major` tells the major ones apart.
Ticks are chosen automatically for the zoom level.
`formatTick` can return an empty string for the labels to hide.
Drawn where you put it; update it with `timeline.update` when it should move.
rows.config: decorations: [{ kind: "now", time: new Date("2026-03-16"), label: "Today" }]

rows.note: A time bar is a slider: drag it, or `Tab` to it and press an arrow. A move is `timeBarMoved` — vis's `timechanged` — and `timeline.timeBars` is where the reader left them.
rows.config: timeBars: [{ id: "deadline", time: new Date("2026-03-25"), label: "Deadline" }]

rows.note: Time runs from right to left, the lane labels and the keyboard's arrows follow. `"auto"` takes the container's `dir`.
A string. Convert numeric ids with `String(id)`.
Plain text. A label that does not fit is shortened with an ellipsis, up to 1 000 items per screen width.
A `Date` or epoch milliseconds — not a string. Convert with `new Date(value)`.
rows.after: timeline.setItems([{ id: "a", laneId: "work", start: new Date("2026-03-03"), end: Date.UTC(2026, 2, 9) }]);

rows.note: Use `className` and a stylesheet; the theme's custom properties style the rest.
Shown on hover and on keyboard focus. The item's accessible name stays its label, the dates and the lane; `hooks.describeItem` changes that.
Moving and resizing are separate.
A dot at its start with a line to the axis. An item without `end` and without a kind is an instant drawn as a thin bar.
rows.after: timeline.setItems([{ id: "p", laneId: "work", kind: "point", start: new Date("2026-03-10"), label: "A point" }]);

rows.note: A labelled band behind every lane; nothing can hit it. A background bound to one group's rows is not here yet.
rows.after: timeline.setItems([...items, { id: "freeze", kind: "background", start: new Date("2026-03-20"), end: new Date("2026-03-27"), label: "Freeze" }]);

rows.note: The item's bar with a line to the axis. Set it per item; there is no timeline-wide default type.
rows.after: timeline.setItems([{ id: "b", laneId: "work", kind: "box", start: new Date("2026-03-12"), label: "A box" }]);

rows.note: Rows inside a group's rows are not supported; nest a group instead (`groups` with `parentId`).

An array of `{ id, label, parentId? }`; a group's `content` is its `label`, and an item names its group with `laneId`. Each group gets a header row you can collapse. Flat `lanes` without headers still work.
rows.after: timeline.update({ groups: [{ id: "work", label: "Engineering" }, { id: "ship", label: "Release" }] });
timeline.update({ groups: [{ id: "work", label: "Engineering" }, { id: "later", label: "Later" }] });

rows.note: Sort the array. A reader can reorder the groups too; that comes out as a `groupCommand`.
rows.after: timeline.update({ groups: [{ id: "ship", label: "Release" }, { id: "work", label: "Engineering" }] });

rows.note: A group names its parent instead of its children. Collapsing is a click on the header, `Enter`, or `timeline.toggleGroup(id)`; a group starts collapsed with `collapsed: true`.
rows.after:
timeline.update({ groups: [{ id: "team", label: "Team" }, { id: "work", label: "Engineering", parentId: "team" }] });
timeline.toggleGroup("team", true);

rows.temporeum: drag a group header, or Alt + arrow
rows.note: Always on; the reorder is reported as a reversible `groupCommand` and the library does not save it.
Lane labels are text.
Move and resize, with a key for every gesture. Every edit is a reversible command.

rows.temporeum: editing: { add, remove, createItem, canAdd, canRemove }
rows.note: A double click on empty row space or `n` adds; the remove handle on a selected item or `Delete` removes. `canAdd` and `canRemove` are synchronous vetoes; `createItem` makes the new item.
rows.config: editing: { enabled: true, add: true, remove: true, canRemove: (item) => item.id !== "locked" }

rows.note: A fixed grid instead of a function.
rows.config: editing: { enabled: true, snapMs: DAY, snapOrigin: new Date("2026-03-01") }

rows.note: A synchronous yes or no for every step of a drag. The finished edit arrives as `itemMoved` with its command.
rows.config: editing: { enabled: true, canMove: (item, next) => next.start === undefined || new Date(next.start).getUTCDay() !== 0 }

rows.note: Open your own editor on a double click.
Or own it: `selectedIds` in the configuration.
`{ ids, previousIds }`.
`{ viewport, reason }`; `viewport.domain` is the window.
One event; its payload says which item, or none.
`command` carries every edit as a reversible command — the undo stack's input.
A time bar is a slider: dragged, or moved with the arrows when it has the focus. The event says where it went, and where it was.
rows.config: timeBars: [{ id: "deadline", time: new Date("2026-03-20"), label: "Deadline" }]
rows.after: timeline.on("timeBarMoved", ({ id, time }) => console.log(id, new Date(time)));
